title: dnstree trace
description: One resolution walked from the root servers down, as dnstree --format json writes it. schema_version is raised whenever a field changes meaning or goes away, never for one that is merely added, so no object here forbids properties it does not name: a reader that understands a version keeps understanding it. A field that carries nothing is left out rather than written empty, so absence is the ordinary case and not an error.

schema_version.description: The version of this document's shape. It is written as a single value rather than a lower bound, because this schema describes that one version: a document of a later version has had a field change meaning or go away, and is not a document this schema can be read against.

elapsed_ms.description: How long the whole walk took. A walk from the root keeps no cache and takes every step itself, so it is the slow way round by design; resolver.elapsed_ms is what it means anything against.

started.description: When the walk began, in RFC 3339. It is what dnssec.signatures is read against, so that a trace read back later says how long its signatures had left when it was made.

resolvers.description: The same question put to recursive servers, in the order the run named them. Several of them is the question asked from several places at once: two that answer differently are two views of one name, and which of them a client gets depends only on which resolver it uses. A server that could not be asked at all is left out rather than carried empty.

root.description: The zone the walk started from. It carries no query of its own: its children are the servers that were asked. Absent when nothing was walked.

warnings.description: What the resolver could not do, in the order it found out.

without.description: What --without told the walk to treat as down: nameserver names, addresses and prefixes, as they were given. The servers inside them were never asked: the walk shows them as not queried, with a note saying which of these left them out, and a check that would have asked one carries an error saying so. An answer the walk found is one the rest of the DNS gives without them.

check.description: The grade --check gave each area of the health of the zone the walk ended in, present only where it asked. Each grade is read off the warnings the walk raised and what --explain says, so an area cannot pass while the flag that checks it warns. Unlike propagation it is read back by --from.

zone.description: The zone the walk ended in.

graded.description: One area of the zone's health and how it came out.

area.description: answer: what the walk came to. delegation: the parent and the zone agree on the nameservers and their glue. consistency: every nameserver serves the same copy of the zone. dnssec: the chain of trust, and what the zone asks its parent. servers: the zone's own servers answer, with authority and room to spare. edns: EDNS and DNS cookies. strangers: zone transfers and recursion, checked only where --check-axfr or --check-recursion asked. caa: who may issue certificates. mail: the MX hosts, DANE, SPF and the mail policies. registration: what the registry holds.

grade.description: passed: checked, and nothing came up. look: worth a look, such as a warning or an unsigned zone, but nothing broken. broken: no answer, or none to trust. skipped: not checked, or nothing there to check.

text.description: What passed, what to look at or what broke; for an area with more than one thing to say, the worst of them.

more.description: How many other things the area had to say, absent where none.

registration.description: What the registry of the domain says about it over RDAP (RFC 9083), present only where --rdap asked, held against the referral the zone above the domain handed the walk. The domain is the zone the walk was delegated to below the TLD, or the TLD and one label of the name where nothing delegated it; the registry is the one IANA's bootstrap file names for the TLD (RFC 9224).

domain.description: The domain the registry was asked about.

server.description: The base URL of the RDAP service asked.

state.description: What the registry said: registered; unregistered, it holds no such domain; unpublished, the TLD runs no RDAP service, or the name is a TLD; unreached, the service could not be asked or did not answer in time.

why.description: What kept the registry from saying more, absent where it answered.

registered.description: When the domain was registered, in RFC 3339, absent where the registry does not say.

expires.description: When the registration runs out, in RFC 3339, absent where the registry does not say. The time left is read against started.

status.description: The registry's statuses (RFC 8056), lowercase, such as client transfer prohibited or server hold.

ds.description: The key tags of the DS records the registry holds.

signed.description: Whether the registry says the delegation is signed.

parent.description: The zone whose referral the registry was held against, absent where the walk was handed none.

ns_only_registry.description: Nameservers the registry holds and the parent did not hand out.

ns_only_parent.description: Nameservers the parent handed out and the registry does not hold.

ds_checked.description: Whether the parent's DS were compared, which takes --dnssec: a referral carries them only then.

ds_only_registry.description: Key tags of DS the registry holds and the parent does not publish.

ds_only_parent.description: Key tags of DS the parent publishes and the registry does not hold.

ds_differ.description: Set where one side has DS and the other none, which is compared where the key tags of both are not to hand.

propagation.description: How long each kind of change to the zone the walk ended in takes to reach every cache, present only where --propagation asked. Each wait is the worst case, a cache filled just before the change, read off TTLs the walk recorded; a change the walk read no TTL for is left out. It is worked out from the rest of the document, and not read back by --from.

zone.description: The zone the walk ended in.

wait.description: How long one kind of change takes to reach every cache.

change.description: answer: the records that answered. denial: a name or type that did not exist, created; the shorter of the SOA's TTL and its minimum (RFC 2308). nameservers: the zone moved to other nameservers; the longer of the parent's NS TTL and the zone's own, read only with --check-ns. ds: the DS at the parent. keys: the zone's DNSKEY set.

type.description: The record type whose TTL decides the wait.

held.description: Each TTL the wait was worked out from, where it was served.
One TTL a wait was worked out from.

field.description: Where the number is not the record's TTL, the field it is: minimum, the last field of an SOA.

trial.description: The delegation --try-ns put in place of a zone's real one, present only where it was asked for. Such a walk is a simulation of the zone moved to these nameservers: the referral to the zone is kept as the parent gave it, DS included, and marked replaced, and the walk goes on to the servers named here instead.

zone.description: The zone whose delegation was replaced.

ns.description: The nameservers named, in order; one named by its address alone is named by the address.

addrs.description: The addresses given for them, which stand in for glue. A nameserver with none was looked up the way one named outside its zone is.

report.description: The failure report --report sent to the agent the zone named (RFC 9567), present only where the chain of trust was bogus, a server of the broken zone named an agent, and --report asked. The report is a TXT lookup of name through a recursive resolver; the lookup arriving is the whole of it.

agent.description: The agent the zone asks failures to be reported to.

name.description: What was looked up, absent where nothing was.

code.description: The extended error reported (RFC 8914): 6, DNSSEC Bogus.

rcode.description: What the lookup came back with.

error.description: Why the report was not sent, or did not get through.

caa.description: Who may issue certificates for the name (RFC 8659), present only where --caa asked. A certificate authority looks for a CAA set at the name, then at each name above it short of the root, and goes by the first it finds, following an alias for that one lookup. The steps that asked are in the tree, as asides.

asked.description: The names looked up, from the name up, until one decided or one failed.

owner.description: The name whose set decides. Absent where none was found, which leaves it to any authority.

records.description: The set that decides, one property each, its value as the zone wrote it.

issue.description: Who may issue for the name. Absent where any authority may; cas is empty where none may.

wildcard.description: Who may issue for a wildcard below the name: the issuewild properties where the set has any, and otherwise the same as issue.

refused.description: Why every authority has to refuse, whatever the set says: a lookup that failed in a zone with a chain of trust behind it, or a critical property nobody knows.

undecided.description: Why the climb could not say who may issue: a lookup that failed where no chain of trust was found behind the zone, which an authority may take as leave to issue, or a budget dnstree ran out of.

dnssec.description: The first verdict on the way up that is not secure, or else the one over the set that decided. A name with no set has to prove it, since dropping a set is all it takes to lift a restriction.

spf.description: The sender policy the name publishes (RFC 7208), present only where --spf asked, as the tree of lookups a receiving mail server makes to check it. The lookups go to a recursive server, the way a mail server makes them, and are not in the tree of the walk. Which term a check stops at depends on who is sending, so every term up to all is followed: this is the check of a sender that matches none of them.

name.description: The name whose policy this is.

server.description: The recursive server the lookups were asked of.

record.description: The policy at the name, its strings joined. Absent where there is none.

terms.description: What the policy says, one term each, in the order it says it.

lookups.description: The terms that cost a DNS lookup, over the whole tree. A check is allowed 10.

void.description: The lookups that found nothing. A check is allowed 2.

cut.description: Present where the query budget or the time ran out, or the check was interrupted, before every term was followed, which leaves lookups and void the least they can be.

result.description: What any check of the policy comes to before the sender is known: ok where nothing in it fails one, none where the name publishes no policy, permerror past a limit or for a policy that does not parse, temperror where a lookup failed, undecided where the budget or the time ran out or the check was interrupted, a policy was too long to read, or no recursive server could be asked.

why.description: What made the result, absent for ok: the first term a check fails at, and why.

mail.description: How mail to the name is delivered, present only where --mail asked, as a sending server that checks DANE finds out (RFC 7672): its MX hosts by preference, the addresses of each, and the TLSA set of each whose addresses are signed, then the MTA-STS, TLS-RPT and DMARC policies beside them. Nothing connects to a mail server, and the MTA-STS policy file is not fetched. Every lookup is a walk of its own, in the tree as an aside.

name.description: The name mail is sent to.

mx.description: The lookup of the MX set.

null.description: Present where the name says it takes no mail, with a null MX (RFC 7505).

implicit.description: Present where the name has no MX set, which makes it its own only host (RFC 5321 5.1).

absent.description: Present where the MX lookup found the name does not exist, so a DMARC policy found above it applies its np rather than its sp (RFC 9989).

hosts.description: The MX hosts by preference, best first, and those of one preference by name.

mta_sts.description: The MTA-STS record at _mta-sts (RFC 8461). Absent where the check stopped before asking.

tls_rpt.description: The TLS-RPT record at _smtp._tls (RFC 8460). Absent where the check stopped before asking.

dmarc.description: The DMARC record at _dmarc of the name, or where the name has none, the one a walk up the tree found for it: at its organisational domain, or at a public suffix marked psd=y (RFC 9989 4.10). A record found above the name applies its np where the name does not exist and its sp where it does, each where it has one, and its p otherwise. Absent where the check stopped before asking, or before the walk could say.

dkim.description: The DKIM keys of the selectors --dkim named, in the order named; selectors the budget left unasked are absent.

stopped.description: Why the check made fewer lookups than it set out to: the MX lookup failed or did not validate, the name does not exist, or a budget ran out. The policies are still looked up unless it was the budget.

cut.description: Present where a budget cut the lookups of the hosts short, which leaves how much DANE covers unknown.

service_path.description: Where a client that reads the name's HTTPS records, or its SVCB records where the question was for those, connects (RFC 9460), present only where --svcb asked: down the alias chain, then to the A and AAAA of every server the last set names. Every lookup other than the walk's own answer is a walk of its own, in the tree as an aside.

chain.description: Each set looked up: the name's own first, then the target of each alias mode record followed.

targets.description: The servers the service mode records of the last set name, each once, best priority first. Where aliases led to a name with no records, that name alone, and fallback is present.

fallback.description: Present where the chain ended on no records, which leaves a client connecting by addresses alone (RFC 9460 3).

none.description: Present where an alias to . says the service does not exist (RFC 9460 2.5.1).

stopped.description: Why the chain was left before its end: a lookup failed or did not validate, the aliases looped or went on past --max-cname, or a budget ran out.

cut.description: Present where a budget cut the address lookups short, which leaves the hints unjudged.

dependencies.description: Every zone the name depends on, present only where --deps asked: the zones the walk was referred to, then those the lookup of each of their nameservers was referred to, in turn, each once. Every lookup is a walk of its own, in the tree as an aside.

zones.description: The zones, the walk's own first, then in the order the lookups came to them. The root is left out.

unresolved.description: The nameservers whose lookup came to no address, which leaves the zones on their way unknown.

stopped.description: Why the lookups were left before every nameserver was looked up, which leaves the list short.

dependency_zone.description: One zone the name depends on.

ns.description: The nameservers its parent delegated it to.

via.description: The nameserver whose lookup came to the zone, absent for a zone on the walk's own way.

for.description: The zone that nameserver serves, absent for a zone on the walk's own way.

dnssec.description: The verdict on the delegation into the zone. Absent without --dnssec.

unresolved_server.description: A nameserver whose lookup came to no address.

error.description: Why: the lookup failed, or the name does not exist.

service_set.description: The HTTPS or SVCB set at one name of the chain.

records.description: The records of the set, each with its parameters decoded.

service_target.description: One server the records name, and what its addresses are.

name.description: The target, the owner of the record where it names .

priority.description: The best priority of the records that name it, 0 for the name a chain of aliases fell back to.

ipv4.description: The lookup of its A set, absent where -6 left it unasked or a budget ran out.

ipv6.description: The lookup of its AAAA set, absent where -4 left it unasked or a budget ran out.

hints.description: The addresses the records naming it hint at.

stray.description: The hints that are none of its addresses, judged only for a family whose lookup was answered.

lookup.description: One name a check looked up after the walk, with a walk of its own.

alias.description: The name the answer came from, where name is an alias.

error.description: Why the lookup failed. Absent where it was answered, even with nothing.

dnssec.description: The first verdict on the way that is not secure, the aliases included, or else the answer's. Absent without --dnssec.

mail_host.description: One MX host, and what DANE does for mail to it.

address.description: The lookup of its addresses: A, or AAAA where it has none or the run asked IPv6 alone.

tlsa.description: The lookup of its TLSA set at _25._tcp, absent where it was not asked.

dane.description: dane, a signed TLSA set a sender can use, so the server's certificate has to match it; unusable, a signed set with no record a sender may use, which still makes it insist on TLS; none, a signed proof there is no set; insecure, addresses or a set nothing signed, which DANE does not apply to; failed, a TLSA lookup that failed or did not validate, which makes a sender that checks DANE treat the host as unreachable; unreachable, no address to deliver to; literal, an address where a host name belongs; unchecked, a set looked up without --dnssec; indeterminate, addresses or a set that could not be checked, for an algorithm or a denial this build cannot check, which a validator reads as unsigned, or for a budget dnstree ran out of.

why.description: What made it so, in a few words.

addresses.description: The addresses its lookup found, absent where it found none.

presented.description: What each address showed --tlsa after STARTTLS, absent where it connected to none.
The certificate one address of an MX host presented, held against the host's TLSA set (RFC 7672 3).

state.description: match, a chain a usable record of the set matches; mismatch, a chain none matches, or a server that offers no STARTTLS, which a sender that checks DANE does not deliver to; unreached, an address the connection or the handshake did not get through to, which could not be checked from where dnstree ran.

subject.description: The subject of the leaf certificate, absent where none was presented.

since.description: When the leaf certificate was issued, in RFC 3339, which is when a key that no longer matches most likely changed.

matched.description: The indexes into the host's records of the ones the chain matches.

why.description: What made it so, in a few words.

tlsa_record.description: One record of a TLSA set (RFC 6698).

data.description: The certificate association data, in lowercase hex.

usable.description: Present where a mail sender may authenticate with it: a trust anchor or end entity record (usage 2 or 3) under a selector and matching type it knows (RFC 7672 3.1).

mail_policy.description: One TXT policy published for mail to the name.

found.description: published, one record of its version; none, no record of its version; invalid, more than one, or one that does not parse, which a sender reads as none; failed, the lookup did not come back with an answer.

tags.description: Its tags in order, the names lowercased.

why.description: What made it invalid or failed, or a reading of it a receiver makes.

dkim_key.description: The key one selector publishes for checking mail signed as the name (RFC 6376 3.6.1).

name.description: Where it was asked: the selector under _domainkey of the name.

found.description: published, one record a key was read from; none, no record, the name an alias leads to missing included; invalid, more than one record, or one a receiver cannot read a key from; failed, the lookup did not come back with an answer, or it did not validate.

tags.description: Its tags in order, the names as written, since DKIM's are case-sensitive.

type.description: The key's algorithm, rsa or ed25519, where it was published.

bits.description: The size of an RSA key, where one was decoded.

state.description: What a receiver makes of a published key: usable; revoked, withdrawn with an empty p=; weak, an RSA key under 1024 bits, or sha1, one that allows only SHA-1, neither of which receivers verify with (RFC 8301).

testing.description: Present where the key is marked t=y, which asks receivers not to hold a failure against the name.

why.description: What made it so, in a few words.

policy_tag.description: One tag=value pair of a policy.

spf_term.description: One mechanism or modifier of a policy, and what it cost.

kind.description: The mechanism or the modifier, lowercase and without its qualifier: all, include, a, mx, ptr, ip4, ip6, exists, redirect, exp, or the name of a modifier nobody defined. Absent for a term that does not parse.

lookup.description: The running count of lookups at this term, absent for one that costs none.

target.description: The name it looks up, as written where it depends on the sender.

record.description: The policy an include or a redirect found at target.

found.description: The addresses an a or an exists found, or the mail servers an mx found, in order of preference.

void.description: Present where the lookup found nothing.

sender.description: Present where the name depends on who is sending (a macro, or ptr), which is counted and not looked up.

unreached.description: Present for a term no check comes to: after all, or a redirect beside one.

problem.description: What is wrong with the term.

fatal.description: Present where the problem fails a check, rather than being advice.

caa_lookup.description: One name a certificate authority asks on the way up.

found.description: none where the name has no set, set where it has one, failed where the lookup did not come back with an answer, which makes every authority refuse.

alias.description: The name the answer came from, where name is an alias.

caa_record.description: One property of the set that decides.

critical.description: The issuer critical flag: an authority that does not know the tag has to refuse.

known.description: Whether the tag is one whose meaning dnstree knows.

cas.description: The authorities, by the domain each identifies itself with.

question.description: What the resolution set out to answer.

resolver.description: The same question put to one recursive server. It is metadata: nothing about the walk depends on it, and a server that would not answer leaves error rather than failing the resolution.

error.description: Why the server could not be asked at all.

match.description: How its answer stands against the one the walk found, absent where there was nothing to compare. The two are allowed to differ honestly: a name tailored to where it is asked from will, since the walk and the resolver are rarely in the same place.

kept.description: What its TTL says of the copy it is serving, absent where it says nothing either way: longer, the walk's answer kept past the TTL the zone gives it; stale, an answer no server of the zone gave the walk, carrying the 30 seconds or less serve-stale hands out (RFC 8767). A reading, not a verdict.

unchecked.description: The same question asked again with checking disabled (RFC 4035), present only where it answered SERVFAIL. A resolver that answers then is one whose validation failed.

failed.description: What its SERVFAIL most likely came of, read against the walk, absent where it did not fail or the walk found no answer: bogus, validation failed on a chain the walk found broken too; validation, it failed validation where the walk did not; cached, a failure it says it is serving from its cache; unreachable, it still failed with checking disabled and said nothing of DNSSEC. A suggestion, not a proof.

authentic.description: The AD bit of its answer: the resolver says it validated what it handed back (RFC 4035). A claim, worth only as much as the path to the resolver.

behaviour.description: What --check-resolver saw the resolver do, present only where it asked, with the answers it rests on.

validates.description: yes, it refused dnssec-failed.org and answered it once told not to check; no, it answered that name and marked not even the root authentic; unknown, the answers leave it open.

rewrites.description: yes, a made-up name under com came back with an address; no, it came back NXDOMAIN; unknown, anything else.

broken.description: dnssec-failed.org. A, asked with DNSSEC, with unchecked present after a SERVFAIL.

root.description: The root's SOA, asked with DNSSEC.

missing.description: The address of the made-up name.

subnet.description: yes, google or akamai was sent a client subnet (ECS, RFC 7871); no, those that answered readably were sent none, which says nothing of other zones; unknown, neither answered readably. Absent from a walk saved before it was asked.

echoes.description: What each of google and akamai saw of the client subnet, for those that answered readably.

minimises.description: yes, internet.nl's test zone saw the name asked a label at a time (RFC 9156); no, it saw the whole name; unknown, it said neither. Absent from a walk saved before it was asked.

google.description: o-o.myaddr.l.google.com. TXT, which reports the address the question came from and any client subnet sent with it.

akamai.description: whoami.ds.akahelp.net. TXT, which reports the same as google, in pairs of strings.

minimisation.description: qnamemintest.internet.nl. TXT, which says in words whether the name was asked a label at a time.

echo.description: What one zone saw of the client subnet. The address is left out: the answer may come from a cache another client filled.

operator.description: Who runs the zone: google or akamai.

bits.description: The prefix length of the subnet, where one was sent.

discovery.description: What the resolver answered for _dns.resolver.arpa (RFC 9462), present only where --ddr asked. Nothing connected to what it offers, so no offer here is verified.

error.description: Why the question could not be asked at all.

designated.description: The encrypted resolvers it designates, in the order they arrived. Absent for a resolver that answered and designates none.
One encrypted resolver a plain one points at.

protocols.description: The transports its ALPN names, of dot, doh and doq. HTTP counts as doh only where a dohpath says where to send the queries.

port.description: Absent where each protocol's default port applies.

dohpath.description: The URI template a doh offer is reached at.

hints.description: The addresses the record says the target is at.

step.description: One query and the queries it led to.

zone.description: The zone the queried server is believed to serve.

kind.description: What the hop turned out to be. The values so far are zone (the synthetic node a trace starts from), referral, answer, cname, nodata (the name exists, the type does not), nxdomain, lame (not serving the zone it was asked about), filtered (an answer somebody decided rather than served, as the server's own extended error says), timeout, error and skipped (known, never queried). It is not written here as a closed set: a kind added later is an addition, and a reader should treat one it does not know as a hop it cannot interpret rather than as a broken document.

proto.description: What the query was carried over: udp, tcp, dot or doh.

start_ms.description: When the hop's first query went out, in milliseconds after started. The hop occupies start_ms to start_ms + rtt_ms, and hops that overlap were in flight together. Present on every hop that asked a server something, zero included, and absent throughout a walk saved before dnstree recorded it.

rtt_ms.description: What the whole hop cost, retries included. Absent where the hop took no measurable time.

size_bytes.description: The answer as it arrived, in bytes on the wire, which is what dig reports as MSG SIZE. Absent where nothing answered.

limit_bytes.description: The most that answer could have been without being truncated: the EDNS0 buffer the query advertised, or the 512 bytes a query carrying no EDNS0 is answered within. Absent over tcp, dot and doh, where a single answer is not bounded this way. A size_bytes near it is a server with no room left: one more record and every resolver asking pays a second round trip over TCP.

tight.description: Set where size_bytes leaves almost nothing of limit_bytes, meaning one more record in the zone truncates the answer. It is the reading of the two sizes, carried so that nothing reading a trace has to hold the margin itself.

records.description: What the server returned, where that is the point of the step.

notes.description: What it took to get the answer: a retry over TCP, a query sent again without EDNS0. They belong to this hop rather than to a new one.

nsid.description: What the server called itself, as RFC 5001 asks it to, absent where the query asked for no identifier or the server published none. It belongs to the answer rather than to the server: one anycast address is many machines, and this says which of them answered. An identifier whose bytes spell no printable name is carried as the hex it arrived as, and one longer than 32 bytes is cut and ends in an ellipsis.

report_to.description: The agent the server asks DNS failures in its zone to be reported to (RFC 9567), absent where it named none. Servers send it unasked, and nothing vouches for it.

cookie.description: How the server answered the DNS cookie the query carried (RFC 7873, --cookie), absent where the query carried none: without --cookie, over DoT and DoH, and on a query asked again without EDNS0. supported is our client cookie back with a server cookie of its own; absent is no cookie at all, which is allowed; mismatch is a client cookie other than the one sent, so the answer may not be the server's; malformed is a cookie of a length no cookie has; rejected is BADCOOKIE even to the server cookie the server handed out itself.

aside.description: Set on work that answers a different question: the address of a nameserver, or the NS set of a zone. The resolution's own answer is never inside one. Following an alias is not an aside: the target is what the question meant all along.

apart.description: Set on the root of a lookup a check made on a walk of its own (--mail, --svcb, the bootstrap signals of --check-ds). The zones under it are somebody else's: what their chains of trust came to is that check's, and never the run's verdict or its exit code.

minimised.description: Set on a hop that asked for less of the name than the walk was after, to find where the next zone cut is (RFC 9156, --qmin). asked says what it put instead, and what it came back with is about that shorter name, so it is never the walk's answer.

compact.description: Set on an nxdomain the server answered as NOERROR, the way a zone that signs as it answers denies a name (RFC 9824): its signed record at the name lists NXNAME, which says the name is not there at all. rcode keeps what the server sent. Only a record the chain of trust found signed earns it.

children.description: The hops this one led to, in the order they were made.

name.description: The name the delegation gave it, absent where only the address is known.

port.description: Where the server was asked. A step of a finished trace always names it.

asn.description: The origin AS of a server address, looked up behind the walk. A prefix announced by more than one AS keeps the first of them. The lookups are best effort and never fail a resolution, so this is absent whenever they could not get through or ran out of time.

allocated.description: The date the prefix was handed out.

flags.description: The header bits worth showing on a hop. Only a bit that is set is written, so reading this is a question of presence: aa (authoritative answer), tc (truncated, the answer did not fit), ad (authenticated data), do (DNSSEC records were asked for) and edns (the server answered with EDNS0).

service.description: An HTTPS or SVCB record decoded. data carries every parameter as text; this is the part something reading the output can branch on.

port.description: The port the record says the service is on, absent where it says none.

hints.description: The ipv4hint and ipv6hint addresses, which a client may connect to before it has looked the target's own up.

ech.description: Whether the record publishes an encrypted client hello configuration. A client that finds one encrypts the name it is about to ask for, which is worth something only if the record reached it unforged.

asked.description: The question one hop put, which is not always the question the resolution set out to answer: a walk asks a zone for its keys, a parent for the DS of a cut, a zone for the NS set it holds of itself, each of its servers for the serial it is on, and the address of a nameserver named somewhere else. It is how a reader tells those apart from the hops the resolution itself is made of, without reading the notes a person reads. Absent on a hop that asked nothing: a server listed and never queried, or a note about why the walk stopped. The class is the document's own and is not repeated here.

soa.description: As much of a zone's start of authority as it is read for. It is present where the zone was asked for it outright, which --serial does of every nameserver, and on a nodata or an nxdomain, which carry the zone's SOA in place of the records they have none of.

serial.description: The version of the zone the answering server is serving. Two nameservers of one zone answering with different serials are answering out of different copies of it. Which of them is the newer is not something to work out by comparing the numbers: serial arithmetic wraps (RFC 1982).

ttl.description: The TTL on the SOA record itself, in seconds.

minimum.description: The last field of the SOA rdata, in seconds. A denial lives for the shorter of this and the TTL on the record (RFC 2308); both are carried, because which of them wins is a reading and this document records what the zone said.

refresh.description: How often the zone's secondaries are told to check for a new copy, in seconds. Absent in a walk saved before it was recorded.

retry.description: How soon a secondary is told to check again after a check failed, in seconds. Absent in a walk saved before it was recorded.

expire.description: How long a secondary that cannot check is told to go on serving its copy before it stops answering for the zone, in seconds. Absent in a walk saved before it was recorded.

delegation.description: The zone cut a referral pointed at.

ttl.description: How long the parent lets the referral be cached, in seconds. It is what a resolver goes on using these nameservers for after they have been changed, which is not the TTL on the answer below them and is usually a great deal longer.

zone_ttl.description: The TTL the zone gives its own NS set, in seconds, present only where --check-ns asked it. The two usually differ, since the parent's is often the registry's to choose, and a resolver that goes by the child's copy once it has one keeps the nameservers for this long instead.

ns.description: The nameserver names, in the order they were received.

glue.description: The addresses from the additional section that this zone was allowed to hand out, meaning the in-bailiwick ones. Bailiwick is judged against the zone the answering server serves, which is what lets the root hand out gTLD server addresses.

zone_addrs.description: The addresses the zone itself gives the nameservers named inside it, set only where --check-ns asked it. The glue is a copy of these, and nothing keeps the two in step: a nameserver renumbered in the zone goes on being handed out at its old address until the registry is told. A name with an empty list is one the zone gives no address of either family.

glueless.description: Nameservers inside the delegated zone that came with no glue. Nothing can resolve them, so the delegation is broken.

out_of_bailiwick.description: Nameservers named outside the delegated zone that came with no address the parent was entitled to give. They are found with a walk of their own instead.

ds_present.description: Whether the parent signed the delegation.

dnssec.description: How far the chain of trust got at one zone cut. A cut is judged from above, so this sits on the step that pointed at the zone rather than on the zone itself: on a referral it is the verdict of the zone in that referral's delegation.

state.description: secure is every link from the anchor down verified; insecure is a parent that proved it publishes no DS; bogus is a chain that breaks; indeterminate is a chain this build could not check, which is never the same as finding it broken.

zone.description: The zone the verdict is about, which is not always the zone of the step it sits on.

algorithm.description: The signing algorithm, so that an algorithm nothing here supports reads differently from a signature that genuinely does not verify.

signatures.description: The signatures a secure verdict rests on, as long as each was made to last: the keys of the zone, the DS its parent signed, the records that answered. Absent on any other verdict. A zone that stops being re-signed goes on validating until the first of them runs out, and then fails all at once.

keys.description: The zone keys of the zone's DNSKEY set, on a secure verdict about entering the zone. They say how it is set up rather than whether it validates.

ds.description: The DS records the parent signed for the zone, on a secure verdict about entering it, each held against the zone's keys. Absent for the root, whose DS are the trust anchors.

keys_ttl.description: The TTL of the zone's DNSKEY set, in seconds, beside keys.

ds_ttl.description: The TTL of the DS set the parent publishes for the zone, in seconds, beside ds.

key.description: One zone key of a DNSKEY set.

sep.description: Flagged as a key signing key.

bits.description: The length of an RSA modulus. Absent for any other algorithm.

pointed.description: A DS of the parent digests to this key.

signs.description: A signature over the DNSKEY set names this key.

ds.description: One DS record a parent publishes for a zone.

digest.description: The digest type, such as SHA256.

match.description: matched where it digests one of the zone's keys, unmatched where it digests none, and unchecked where its digest type cannot be computed here, which says nothing either way.

probe.description: Set on the aside that asked a nameserver of the zone the walk ended in for what it should keep from strangers, with --check-axfr or --check-recursion. Nothing of what it gave is kept.

kind.description: transfer is the whole zone asked for by AXFR; recursion is a name outside its zones asked with recursion desired.

state.description: open where the server gave it, closed where it did not, and unchecked where it could not be asked, which says nothing either way.

edns.description: Set on the aside that asked a nameserver of the zone the walk ended in for the zone's SOA in one of the shapes RFC 8906 tests, with --check-edns.

kind.description: edns is EDNS0 and nothing else, the baseline; version is EDNS version 1, to be answered BADVERS; option is option 100 and flag is flag 0x40, neither defined, to be ignored and not copied back.

state.description: ok where the server answered as RFC 6891 says it must, broken where it did not, and unchecked where it did not answer the baseline, which says nothing about the rest.

fault.description: What a broken answer got wrong: silent is no answer where the baseline got one, rcode the wrong rcode (the step's own), no-opt no OPT record, version an OPT record of a version other than 0, no-soa NOERROR without the SOA, echoed the option or flag copied back, answer BADVERS with the SOA anyway.

dangling.description: Set on the hop that showed a name left pointing at something that is not there, which whoever creates that thing first can answer for. It says what the walk saw: a zone halfway through a move looks the same.

kind.description: nameserver: a nameserver whose name does not exist. alias: an alias whose target does not exist. lame: every nameserver of the zone answered without authority for it, which is how a hosting service answers for a zone nobody has created there.

name.description: What was left pointing: the zone delegated, or the alias.

target.description: What it points at: the nameserver, or the alias's target. Absent for lame.

missing.description: The name zone says does not exist: target or the ancestor of it directly below zone, and what somebody else would have to create there. Absent for lame.

zone.description: The zone whose denial says missing does not exist. Absent for lame.

nsec3.description: How the zone that denied something hashes its names (RFC 5155), read off an NSEC3 whose signature held. Absent where no NSEC3 was checked. RFC 9276 asks for no extra iterations and no salt.

zone.description: The zone that owns the NSEC3, which is the parent where it proved it publishes no DS.

iterations.description: The extra times each name is hashed.

salt.description: The salt, in hex. Absent for none.

signal.description: What the zone asks its parent to publish, in its CDS and CDNSKEY records (RFC 7344, RFC 8078), held against the DS the parent publishes. Present where --check-ds asked, on the verdict of the cut the DS belongs to.

state.description: none is a zone that proved it asks for nothing; match asks for the keys the parent holds; pending asks for another key than the parent holds: a rollover waiting on the parent, or, from a zone the parent holds no DS for, its first DS, which bootstrap says whether a parent would add; delete asks for no DS at all; inconsistent is a CDS and a CDNSKEY describing different keys, which a parent acts on neither of; unchecked is a request that could not be fetched, or was not signed by the zone's keys.

requested.description: The key tags the zone asks for.

held.description: The key tags the parent's DS names.

csync.description: What the zone asks its parent to copy from it, in its CSYNC record (RFC 7477): its NS set, the addresses of the nameservers named inside it, or both. Present where --check-ns asked.

state.description: none is a zone with no CSYNC; ready is a signed one a parent that polls acts on; manual is signed but waits for whoever runs the parent to approve it; waiting is signed but waits for the zone's serial to reach its own; unproven is not signed, or its signature did not hold, and no parent acts on it; unchecked could not be fetched, or its signature was not checked without --dnssec.

immediate.description: Whether a parent may act on it without asking anyone.

soaminimum.description: Whether it waits for the zone's serial to reach serial.

types.description: The types it asks to be copied, as the record names them.

zone_serial.description: The serial of the SOA the zone served beside it, where soaminimum made it matter.

changes.description: What a parent acting on it would add to or remove from the delegation the walk was handed, whether or not one would act on it.

bootstrap.description: Whether a parent would add the first DS of a zone that is signed but not yet secure (RFC 9615): the operator of each nameserver named outside the zone has to publish the zone's CDS and CDNSKEY under _dsboot.<zone>._signal.<nameserver>, in a zone of its own that validates. Present on the signal of a zone its parent holds no DS for that asks for a key.

state.description: ready is every signal validating and saying what the zone does; refused is a parent that bootstraps adding no DS; unchecked is a signal that could not be looked up.

signals.description: One per nameserver the parent delegates to, in its order.

delegation_change.description: One record of a delegation a parent would add or remove.

add.description: true for a record added, false for one removed.

data.description: The address, absent for an NS.

bootstrap_signal.description: The bootstrap signal under one nameserver.

name.description: Where the signal was looked for, absent where no name could be made.

state.description: matched validates and says what the zone does; differs validates and asks for something else; missing is a signal the operator's zone proves is not there; unproven did not validate; failed is a lookup that failed or was cut short; unasked is a nameserver named inside the zone, which a parent does not ask, or one whose signal would need a name longer than 255 octets.

requested.description: The key tags the signal asks for.

signature.description: How long one signature was made to last, in RFC 3339. One with less than a fifth of that left when the walk was made is late in its life, which is what a stopped signer leaves behind.

extended_error.description: What a server said about its own answer, in the codes of RFC 8914. An rcode says what happened; this says why, and it is the only thing in a reply that tells an answer withheld apart from an answer that is not there.

reason.description: The registered name of the code, absent for one this build does not know.

text.description: EXTRA-TEXT, whatever the server chose to add in words, whole. Every byte outside printable ASCII, and the backslash, is escaped as \DDD or \\.

withheld.description: Set where the code says somebody decided this answer rather than served it, so that a reader need not carry the list of which codes those are.

subnet.description: The client subnet of RFC 7871 as a server handed it back. A server that answers with one has taken it into account.

scope.description: How much of the prefix the server actually used. Zero is a server saying this answer is the same for everybody.
